correctness.rationale: For all nonnegative row-stochastic matrices, the row-total-variation identity bounds each weighted-coordinate difference by delta(W) times the diameter. The hyperbolic identity for logistic secants gives exactly tanh(beta delta R/4) as the optimal maximal difference, even under arbitrary shared measurable forcing. The invariant cube supports global Caratheodory solutions, the diameter inequality holds almost everywhere, and scalar ODE comparison yields the result at all times. A symmetric two-node system has constant mid-state 1/2 and saturates every inequality for every q and initial diameter. At q=4, differentiation of r^(-2) yields derivative asymptotic 2/3, hence t r^2 tends to 3/2. Above q=4 strict concavity gives a unique nonzero scalar root, realized by exact unequal network equilibria. A self-contained Python checker independently ran 4000 Dini, 1500 saturation, 9 critical and 4 supercritical finite diagnostics; these are not substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: Row overlap d(W) is a natural mixing invariant for heterogeneous activation in threshold networks. The result proves nontrivial global coordinate synchronization even when feedback beta exceeds the regime of full-state uniqueness, and yields the optimal nonlinear bound for every state diameter and arbitrary shared forcing. Its critical t^(-1/2) coefficient and equality witness provide a sharp boundary and meaningful network/topology separation. It is a structured qualitative and quantitative theorem about a motivated family of networks rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or mere replication of a known table.
